title: The notification centre inbox lists the last N days of notifications and each acknowledge control round-trips to the server
description: The applying project renders a notification-centre route (default `/notifications-centre`, operator-elicited) whose inbox surface lists the notifications delivered in the last N days per the ADR-2103 retention window (default thirty days, elicited). Each notification carries a stable `data-notification-id` attribute the pack enumerates by (never by a role attribute alone, per the T-3 gate discipline), and each carries a keyboard-reachable acknowledge control (`[data-action="acknowledge"]`) plus a mark-read control (`[data-action="mark-read"]`); the surface offers one mark-all-read control (`[data-action="mark-all-read"]`) reachable in reading order. Activating the acknowledge control POSTs an acknowledge request to the applying project's server, the server responds, and the DOM updates in response: the notification's `data-acknowledged` reads `true` after the round-trip. Every item is Tab-reachable from the start of the surface without a mouse.
rationale: A transient toast is not a system of record; the notification centre is. Making the centre the operator's inbox with a retention window and per-item acknowledge round-trip is what turns a fleeting on-screen message into a durable one the operator can return to and confirm. Enumerating items by `data-notification-id` rather than by `role="listitem"` on the container follows the T-3 gate discipline: a role attribute the primary element carries alone does not enumerate multiple children; a per-element data attribute does.
